_note: SLIP publishes tissue vocabularies only for its own datasets (TCGA lung, DHMC, PatchGastricADC22). This vocabulary is authored for this benchmark in the released format ('Name: description'), reusing the organ-independent phenotypes from text_prompts/slip/TCGA_tissues.json and replacing the lung-specific ones. A SLIP result on this cohort is not prompt-faithful.
tissues: Terminal duct lobular unit: Clustered small acini around an intralobular duct, lined by luminal and myoepithelial layers.
Myoepithelial layer: Continuous outer rim of flattened cells beneath the basement membrane of ducts and acini.
Ductal carcinoma in situ: Malignant epithelium filling ducts while confined by an intact basement membrane.
Tubule formation: Neoplastic cells arranged as recognisable glandular lumina.
Single-file infiltration: Tumour cells infiltrating in linear chains between collagen fibres.
Desmoplastic stroma: Dense fibroproliferative stroma provoked by invasive carcinoma.
Adipose tissue: Sheets of clear univacuolated adipocytes with compressed peripheral nuclei.
Tumor nests: Clusters of cancerous cells forming distinct groups separated by stroma.
Solid tumor: A solid sheet of cancer cells with little intervening architecture.
Stroma: Supporting connective tissue between tumour and normal structures.
Necrosis: Areas of dead cells with loss of nuclear detail and granular debris.
Inflammatory infiltrate: Immune cells scattered through tissue in response to injury or tumour.
Vascular invasion: Tumour cells within the lumen of a blood or lymphatic vessel.
Fibrosis: Dense collagen deposition replacing normal tissue architecture.
Pleomorphism: Marked variation in nuclear size, shape and staining between tumour cells.
Lymphocytic infiltration: Dense aggregates of small mature lymphocytes.
Hyalinization: Homogeneous glassy eosinophilic material replacing stroma.
